learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply necessary legislation in the practice of the Industrial Technical Engineer profession.
Adequate knowledge of the concept of a company, its institutional and legal framework. Organization and management of companies.

Knows and documents a quality management system applicable to a productive company, standardized according to ISO 9001 or other international standards (EFQM, and others), and similarly documents integrated management systems and quality management systems for industrial testing/calibration laboratories.
Plans and deploys quality management objectives and undertakes audits of quality management systems and the processes documented within them.
Applies techniques of control, assurance, quality management, total quality, and continuous improvement of products and processes throughout their life cycle.
Identifies product standardization and certification needs, as well as legal product safety requirements, and evaluates their compliance.

Knows and selects appropriate inspection and verification methods (including statistical process control, experimental design, reliability, etc.) based on criteria such as the manufacturing system used or established quality objectives.

assessment_rules: The use of unpermitted materials or electronic devices during an assessment test may result in the immediate withdrawal of the exam and a failing grade (numerical mark '0' on the test). Additionally, the responsible professor may complete the corresponding report and submit it for consideration of disciplinary action for academic fraud. If it is a continuous assessment exam, the student cannot continue, unless stated otherwise in the academic guide. If it is a regular or extraordinary call exam, disciplinary proceedings will result in a 'pending resolution' grade until the file is closed.
